source_spans.locator: Annual Review of Neuroscience 24, published p.167, Abstract: active maintenance of goal/means patterns in prefrontal cortex provides modulatory signals that guide neural activity along task-appropriate mappings

Annual Review of Neuroscience 24, published pp.171-172, Overview of the Theory and illustrative context-dependent action example: maintained PFC representations bias downstream pathways and support the context-appropriate response when stronger alternatives compete

Annual Review of Neuroscience 24, published p.173, Minimal Requirements for a Mechanism of Top-Down Control: PFC as active memory in the service of control; robust maintenance, flexible updating, and influence over task-relevant neural pathways
Annual Review of Neuroscience 24, published pp.179-180, Active Maintenance: task-rule activity must persist beyond the eliciting event and across intervening potentially interfering events

Annual Review of Neuroscience 24, published pp.183-185, Guided Activation account and Stroop model: PFC control units modulate rather than transmit input-output mappings, biasing weaker task-relevant pathways when they compete with stronger alternatives

conditions: task performance requires a context-appropriate mapping among inputs, internal states, and outputs, especially when the relevant pathway is weak, ambiguous, rapidly changing, or competes with a stronger habitual alternative
population: human and nonhuman primate systems reviewed by the source, together with computational models used to illustrate the proposed mechanism
substrate: prefrontal cortical representations and downstream cortical/subcortical processing pathways
task: maintain and apply a current goal or rule so that processing follows the task-appropriate pathway
temporal_scope: the goal/rule representation is activated in advance of and maintained over the interval in which it must bias processing, potentially persisting beyond the eliciting event and across intervening distractors

nodes.description: prefrontal subsystem proposed to actively maintain task-relevant goal and rule representations and provide modulatory top-down signals
other cortical or subcortical systems in which input/internal-state-to-output processing pathways carry task performance
persisting pattern of prefrontal activity representing a current goal, rule, or means for achieving the goal
modulatory signal generated by the maintained prefrontal representation that alters support for downstream processing pathways
activity flowing along the downstream pathway that implements the mapping appropriate to the current goal or rule
a stronger, more habitual, or otherwise competing pathway that would dominate without sufficient top-down modulation
behavioral or internal output produced by the task-appropriate downstream mapping

relations.description: the source assigns active maintenance of current goals, rules, and means to patterns of activity in the prefrontal subsystem
maintained prefrontal representations provide top-down modulatory signals to other brain structures
the modulatory signal changes downstream processing so that activity is preferentially guided along the pathway appropriate to the current task
when a stronger competing pathway is present, producing the task-appropriate output depends on sufficient activation of the task-relevant pathway under top-down support
the source explicitly distinguishes the prefrontal role as modulatory from the downstream pathways that actually transmit the input/internal-state-to-output mapping
